newsitem.title: MEXICO: One third of Mexicans say guerrilla violence OK.
newsitem.headline: One third of Mexicans say guerrilla violence OK.

text.p: Almost one third of Mexicans believe that a new guerrilla group operating a various southern states is justified in using violence, a poll published Friday said.

The poll, carried out by Mexico City daily Reforma and Monterrey sister paper El Norte, discovered that 30 percent of the population said the self-styled Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) is right to take up arms.
Pollsters questioned 980 people in Mexico City, Guadalajara and Monterrey, Mexico's capital and second and third cities. No margin of error was given.

Leftist EPR rebels sprang up on June 28 calling for the overthrow of the government. Since then, the guerrillas have attacked military and police bases in several states and claim to have killed 27 people, mostly army personnel or police.
A majority 64 percent of those polled said the rebel actions were not justified, five percent said they were not sure and one percent did not answer.
Of those polled, 32 percent said violence is justified when there is injustice and 63 percent said political change does not justify violence.
On the army, 56 percent said troops should intervene in the conflict and 37 percent said they should not intervene, while 7 percent answered they were not sure.
